learning_outcomes.text: Understand and use basic English expressions for everyday situations.
Read and comprehend short and simple texts.
Introduce themselves, ask and answer simple questions.
Demonstrate correct use of basic grammar structures.

syllabus_topics: Unit 1 – Nice to meet you! (Pages 4–9) Vocabulary: Countries Grammar: Statements and questions with be Pronunciation: Syllable stress Conversation: Introduce your partner Topics/Skills: Making introductions, asking personal questions

Unit 2 – What do you do? (Pages 10–15) Vocabulary: Jobs Grammar: The simple present Pronunciation: Reduction of do you Conversation: Talk about what you and your family do Topics/Skills: Talking about jobs, describing what people do

Unit 3 – Do you like noodles? (Pages 16–21) Vocabulary: Food Grammar: The simple present (questions with do) Pronunciation: Question intonation Conversation: Choose what you want to eat Topics/Skills: Likes and dislikes, ordering food

Unit 4 – How often do you exercise? (Pages 24–29) Vocabulary: Sports Grammar: Frequency adverbs Pronunciation: Final s sounds Conversation: Ask your partner about exercise habits Topics/Skills: Talking about habits and routines

Unit 5 – I’m listening to music. (Pages 30–35) Vocabulary: Daily activities Grammar: The present continuous Pronunciation: Reduction of what is and what are Conversation: Ask what your partner is doing right now Topics/Skills: Talking about current actions, describing what people are doing

Unit 6 – Where were you yesterday? (Pages 36–41) Vocabulary: Problems Grammar: The past tense of be Pronunciation: Pronunciation of wasn’t and weren’t Conversation: Tell your partner why you were late Topics/Skills: Talking about past events, describing problems

Unit 7 – Which one is cheaper? (Pages 44–49) Vocabulary: Clothes Grammar: Comparative adjectives Pronunciation: Word stress in comparisons Conversation: Choose two things and ask which one your partner prefers Topics/Skills: Talking about clothes, comparing prices and items

Unit 8 – They’re very friendly. (Pages 50–55) Vocabulary: Appearance and personality Grammar: Be like and look like Pronunciation: Linking does and is in questions Conversation: Describe someone you know Topics/Skills: Describing people’s appearance and personality traits

Unit 9 – You can visit the zoo. (Pages 56–61) Vocabulary: Local attractions Grammar: Can and can’t Pronunciation: Reduction of can Conversation: Choose a city and talk about what you can do there Topics/Skills: Talking about tourist attractions and things to do

Unit 10 – Is there a coffee shop? (Pages 64–69) Vocabulary: Places around town Grammar: There is and There are Pronunciation: Word stress in compound nouns Conversation: Ask about shops and places in your city Topics/Skills: Asking for and giving directions, talking about city facilities

Unit 11 – I had a good time. (Pages 70–75) Vocabulary: Vacation activities Grammar: The simple past Pronunciation: Reduction of did you Conversation: Ask your partner about vacations and experiences Topics/Skills: Talking about past experiences and vacations

Unit 12 – I’m going to go by car. (Pages 76–81) Vocabulary: Transport Grammar: Be going to + verb Pronunciation: Reduction of going to Conversation: Talk about travel plans and how to get around Topics/Skills: Talking about future plans and transportation
